findings.title: Recurring calendar deletions are not awaited and can be missed
findings.body: The recurring cancellation branch uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promise, so execution reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 before these async callbacks have resumed and populated `apiDeletes`. Recurring booking calendar events may never be deleted before the handler returns, and any rejected `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` promise is unhandled. This regressed because the callback previously used synchronous `getCalendar` and pushed into `apiDeletes` synchronously. Use `for...of` or `Promise.all` and await the deletions.

findings.title: Reschedule cancellation runs in unawaited async forEach
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` does not await the async callbacks. The mutation continues to send reschedule emails and webhooks and can return before the old calendar/video events are cancelled; rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` also become unhandled. Use an actual `for...of`/`Promise.all` and await before sending the follow-up emails.

findings.title: Unawaited async forEach can leave Vital calendar events uncancelled
findings.body: The async callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` awaits `getCalendar` but `forEach` does not await the returned promise. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from the async callback, and `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` runs before the cancellation work completes. Replace this with a `for...of` loop or collect and `await Promise.all(...)` for the cancellation promises.

findings.title: Unawaited async forEach can leave WipeMyCal calendar events uncancelled
findings.body: Same issue as in the vital reschedule helper: the async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited, so the function can send reschedule emails and return before `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent` finish. Errors from the async callback are unhandled. Use an `await`-able loop or `Promise.all`.

findings.title: Storing `import()` promises still eagerly loads every app
findings.body: Each property is an executed `import()` call, so when this module is evaluated all app modules start loading/evaluating even if no caller ever accesses that app. That undercuts the intended lazy loading and can cause a large prefetch/cold-start cost; an import failure for an unused app can also become an unhandled rejection. Store thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke them at the lookup sites if on-demand loading is desired.
